ideas.title: Design-for-Duty: Engineer Below the 15% Metal Line
ideas.one_liner: A CAD/BOM tool that redesigns imported products to fall under Section 232's metal-weight cliffs or qualify for the 10% US-melt rate.
ideas.customer: Product-engineering and sourcing leads at $20M-$500M brands that import metal-heavy goods (furniture, fitness gear, grills, hand tools, lighting, enclosures, HVAC accessories).
ideas.problem: Since 2026-04-06 metals duties apply to full customs value: 50% on primary metal, 25% on derivatives, and 10% if made with US-melted steel or US-smelted aluminum/copper. Products under 15% metal weight are excluded (per Foley; verify current text). More derivative articles were proposed on 2026-08-06. Insiders treat this as a sourcing or lobbying problem. Brokers and freight forwarders cannot change a bill of materials, and engineers do not know the cliff exists.
ideas.solution: A plugin and standalone tool that ingests CAD mass properties and the BOM (SolidWorks, Fusion, Onshape or CSV). It computes metal weight share per SKU and simulates variants, such as a polymer or wood part in place of a steel bracket, or one US-melted component. It returns duty-weighted landed cost per variant and drafts the engineering change order. It also flags SKUs sitting just above a tier boundary.
ideas.why_now: The IEEPA tariffs fell on 2026-02-20 and the regime moved onto Section 232. Metal content is now the biggest variable in landed cost. Full-value duties began in April 2026, and the August 2026 proposal adds derivative products.
ideas.revenue_model: SaaS at $1.5-4k a month per product line. Launch-phase audits at $1.5k per SKU. Optional 10-15% share of first-year duty saved on redesigned SKUs.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: The tariff is a bill-of-materials problem, not a country problem. A few points of mass shifted can be worth more than moving a factory, and no one in the chain (broker, freight forwarder, sourcing agent) is paid to touch the design.
ideas.first_30_days: Pull public bill-of-lading data for HTS chapters exposed to metal derivatives. Cold-email 100 product heads offering a free one-SKU cliff check. Sell 10 fixed-price SKU audits at $1.5k, done in a spreadsheet. Retain a customs attorney to confirm how metal weight is measured. Build the plugin once patterns repeat.

ideas.title: Amps Not Acres: Power Headroom for Retrofits
ideas.one_liner: Headroom reports and a load-sequencing kit that let plants add machines inside existing walls without a new transformer.
ideas.customer: Owners and plant managers of 20-300 employee manufacturers, and machine-tool, compressor and robot dealers who need to know whether a customer can power what they sell.
ideas.problem: Site selectors and economic developers think reshoring is limited by land, buildings and permits. The data say otherwise. Factory construction is down 22-32% from peak, yet nondefense capital-goods orders hit a record $85.9B in July, so equipment is going into old buildings. Transformer and switchgear prices are up 89-96% since 2019 as data centers compete for the same gear. Utility service upgrades cost six figures and take a year or more.
ideas.solution: Step 1 is a Headroom Report. It pulls 12 months of utility interval data (Green Button) and uses measured demand (NEC 220.87 allows this) to show how many kW can be added, ready for a PE stamp. Step 2 is a clamp-on CT and PLC/gateway kit that staggers compressors, furnaces, welders and spindle start-ups to cap demand peaks. Step 3 adds an optional battery or thermal-storage partner for the residual gap.
ideas.why_now: Record capital-goods orders with $953B unfilled, prices for electrical gear up sharply, and reshoring that is happening in existing buildings. No incumbent sells 'create amps in software' to a 50-person shop.
ideas.revenue_model: $1.5-3k per report (dealers pay to close sales). $5-15k for hardware and install. $200-400 a month for monitoring. Referral fees from dealers and battery vendors.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: Nameplate capacity is not the constraint. Measured coincident peak is, and it is usually far below service rating. The scarce input is amps, and amps can be created by sequencing loads.
ideas.first_30_days: Pitch 10 machine dealers on the report as a free pre-sale add-on. Get interval data from 5 plants. Partner with a licensed PE for stamping. Assemble the first controller from off-the-shelf CTs and a PLC.

ideas.title: Spindle-Hour Options: Reserve Capacity, Skip Inventory
ideas.one_liner: Standardized capacity-reservation contracts that let OEMs hedge supply risk by paying a small premium for guaranteed machining hours.
ideas.customer: Procurement leads at $50M-$1B OEMs (industrial equipment, medical devices, defense subcontractors) and 10-100 person job shops with idle spindles.
ideas.problem: 57% of negative ISM comments cite price volatility, and one respondent called lead times worse than the pandemic era. Machine-shop owners report buying a full year of inventory to lock in prices. That ties up cash and risks obsolescence. Marketplaces sell only spot capacity, and shops cannot get predictable base load.
ideas.solution: A standard reservation contract by machine class (3-axis, 5-axis, Swiss, wire EDM, weld cell). The buyer pays a reservation fee for N hours a month over 6-12 months at a strike rate, with materials indexed to published metals prices. The buyer exercises by releasing drawings within 10 days. The platform vets shops, holds deposits in escrow, and resells unexercised hours to spot buyers.
ideas.why_now: Metals repricing under Section 232, Hormuz freight shocks, machinery hiring picking up, and auto-supplier capacity going idle. Buyers can no longer count on spot capacity appearing.
ideas.revenue_model: 6-10% of reservation fees plus 2-3% of exercised work. Later, underwrite a portfolio of options for the spread.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: A job shop's most valuable asset is certainty of base load, and it will discount 10-20% for take-or-pay. Buyers fear not getting parts more than they fear price. An option on capacity is a cheaper hedge than a year of inventory, and the deposit doubles as working capital for the shop.
ideas.first_30_days: Recruit 8-10 shops with one machine class in one region (for example Northeast Ohio). Draft a two-page contract with a manufacturing lawyer. Pitch 15 buyers who are already stockpiling inventory. Aim for $50k in reservations by day 60. Run it as a brokerage first.

ideas.title: Tariff Surcharge Clawback for Downstream Buyers
ideas.one_liner: A contingency recovery-audit firm that claws back tariff surcharges buyers paid on duties their suppliers have since had refunded.
ideas.customer: CFOs, AP and purchasing teams at $20M-$1B manufacturers and distributors that paid itemized supplier 'tariff surcharges' in 2025-26.
ideas.problem: The Supreme Court struck down the IEEPA tariffs on 2026-02-20. By 2026-07-10 CBP had accepted about $121.75B in claims and repaid about $86.3B. Many suppliers billed explicit surcharges (one shop-floor post cites 2.7%) to fund those duties, and they are now collecting refunds on the same money. Buyers assume the refund belongs to the importer of record, and AP treats surcharge lines as noise.
ideas.solution: Ingest 18 months of AP data from the ERP or QuickBooks. Use LLM extraction on invoices and price-increase emails to find surcharge lines. Rank suppliers by likely refunded exposure (product HTS and the IEEPA rate window). Generate credit-memo demands and negotiation scripts. Escalate to counsel only for large amounts. Recovery depends on invoice and contract language, and most cases settle as credits against future invoices.
ideas.why_now: Refunds are paying out in phases right now, so suppliers hold the cash today. Contract dispute windows are open and evidence is fresh.
ideas.revenue_model: 20-30% contingency fee on recovered cash or credits. Optional $5k flat fee for a scan of the last 12 months of AP.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: The strongest and cheapest claim to a refund often belongs to the downstream buyer holding an itemized surcharge, not the importer. Recovery-audit firms hunt duplicate payments, not tariffs. Buyers also avoid asking for fear of damaging the supplier relationship, so an anonymous third party has an edge.
ideas.first_30_days: Sign 5 mid-market manufacturers for a free 12-month surcharge scan. Have counsel draft one template letter. Send the first demands and measure realized recovery. First credit memos should land within 60-90 days.

ideas.title: Keep the 58-Year-Old Machinist Two Years Longer
ideas.one_liner: Carrier-co-funded ergonomic and assistive-tech programs that delay retirements instead of chasing new hires.
ideas.customer: Manufacturers with 30-300 employees and an older workforce. Workers' comp carriers and brokers co-fund it through loss-control budgets and premium credits.
ideas.problem: The industry chases Deloitte and Manufacturing Institute's 3.8M hires needed by 2033, with 1.9M possibly unfilled. Their 2024 report stresses retention, not just applicants. About 60% of manufacturing firms have owners aged 55+. Each retiring senior machinist takes years of tacit skill, and recruiting and training replacements is slow and costly.
ideas.solution: A 90-day Longevity Program. It starts with an ergonomic assessment of every role held by workers aged 50+. Then it installs a kit of lift assists, tilting fixtures, better lighting and vibration-damped tool holders, plus optional exoskeleton pilots for overhead work. It also designs phased-retirement roles (for example, mentor three days a week). It tracks injuries and retention against a baseline.
ideas.why_now: Manufacturing jobs are up 58k since the December 2025 low, so labor is tightening. Announced reshoring hires land 12-24 months after announcements. Lift-assist and exoskeleton hardware is now cheap enough for small shops.
ideas.revenue_model: $8-25k per program plus about $150 per employee per month for monitoring and a training-video library. Finder fees from carriers. Optional performance pricing tied to retention.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: The cheapest hire is the one who does not retire. Insurers already fund loss control for exactly this age group, so the shop's cost is partly paid by a third party with a matching incentive. My rough estimate is that one avoided senior-machinist retirement is worth well over $100k in replacement, scrap and customer risk.
ideas.first_30_days: Call loss-control reps at three regional workers' comp carriers or brokers. Offer three free shop assessments. Document before-and-after injury and absence data. Use the results to sell paid programs to the shops.

ideas.title: Tooling Hostage: Repatriate Molds and Dies
ideas.one_liner: Extract molds, dies and fixtures from Asian suppliers, refurbish them, and re-home them with US or nearshore shops.
ideas.customer: Consumer-product and industrial OEMs with $10M-$500M revenue and $50k-$2M of tooling sitting at Asian contract manufacturers, plus the new US or Mexican shops that will use it.
ideas.problem: Tariffs, a USMCA that was not renewed, and a war shock (freight up to 50%) push companies to move production. The first blocker is the tooling. Ownership is ambiguous, suppliers demand payoffs, drawings are missing, and nobody handles inspection, crating, freight and requalification as one service.
ideas.solution: Step 1 is a fixed-fee Tool Audit covering contract review, inspection video, location, condition and cost to escape. Step 2 is turnkey extraction: a local agent and letter, crating, freight and a customs review of the tooling's duty class. Step 3 is US refurbishment and first-article requalification through partner shops. Step 4 is a scan-and-drawing escrow so the next move is easy.
ideas.why_now: Companies are re-sourcing now under the rebuilt tariff regime. Freight and war-risk surcharges make each move costly, and the first-mover on tool logistics is unclaimed territory.
ideas.revenue_model: Audit at $2.5-5k. Extraction at $8-40k or 10-15% of tooling value. Refurbishment and requalification pass-through at about 15% margin. Escrow subscription.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: The lock-in in Asia is the tool, not cheap labor, and the tool's legal owner is often unclear. Whoever holds the tool controls the reshoring decision, so extraction is the real first step. Duty treatment of imported tooling and Chinese export or IP disputes need counsel.
ideas.first_30_days: Publish a 'Where are your tools?' checklist. Run 5 audits for hardware brands found via trade shows and Amazon brand lists. Hire a fixer and lawyer in Shenzhen or Ningbo. Line up one refurbishment partner shop in Ohio or Michigan.

ideas.title: Time-to-First-Part: Install Readiness for Machine Dealers
ideas.one_liner: A pre-delivery site-scan and commissioning package that gets backlogged machines cutting parts weeks sooner.
ideas.customer: Machine-tool, laser and robot dealers and OEM sales teams, plus 20-200 employee manufacturers buying their first big machine.
ideas.problem: Unfilled capital-goods orders sit at $953B after a record $85.9B in July orders. Much of it lands in old buildings with no as-built drawings. Machines arrive to floors, doors, crane paths and utility drops that cannot take them, so crated $500k machines sit idle. Dealers often get paid only at acceptance.
ideas.solution: A 20-minute phone or LiDAR walkthrough becomes an as-built model. Software checks the machine footprint, door and aisle clearance and rigging path, flags slab and vibration issues (with a ground-penetrating-radar partner), lists air, coolant and chip-handling needs, and produces a rigging plan and punch list. It can also dispatch vetted riggers and millwrights.
ideas.why_now: Reshoring is happening inside existing walls, the equipment backlog is at a record, and riggers and millwrights are scarce. Phone-based 3D capture (LiDAR, Gaussian splats) has matured.
ideas.revenue_model: $1.2-3k per site package, paid by the dealer or bundled into the machine price. 10-15% referral on rigging. Dealer team subscriptions.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: Dealers get paid at acceptance, so time-to-first-part is their cash-flow metric and they will pay to shorten it. The unfilled-order backlog hides a second backlog of installed-but-not-producing machines.
ideas.first_30_days: Sign three regional dealers (CNC, laser or robot) for a pilot. Do 10 scans with iPhones. Produce a sample report. Measure install days saved against comparable installs.

ideas.title: Supplier-Owned Origin Passport for Tier-2 Shops
ideas.one_liner: A portable, supplier-owned origin and metal-content passport that answers every customer's questionnaire once.
ideas.customer: Tier-2 and tier-3 suppliers with 10-200 employees in the US, Mexico and Canada. Buyers pay for portfolio dashboards.
ideas.problem: USMCA was not renewed on 2026-07-01 and now faces annual reviews through 2036. USTR flagged simplified compliance for smaller suppliers. CBP is prioritizing origin verification. Full-value duties depend on HTS class, metal weight and melt origin per SKU. Every buyer sends a different spreadsheet, and small suppliers re-answer them all with errors that expose buyers to penalties.
ideas.solution: Guided intake for BOM, mill certs (melt and pour country extracted from MTR PDFs), HTS and USMCA tariff-shift or regional-content calculation, kept as a versioned, signed record. The supplier shares subsets with each buyer by link. Buyers get standardized machine-readable packets and alerts when rules change. The first buyer is free, and suppliers pay to share with more.
ideas.why_now: Annual USMCA reviews create a permanent audit cycle, CBP is focused on origin verification, and Section 232 tiers now depend on melt origin. Regulators are asking for less burdensome small-supplier compliance.
ideas.revenue_model: $99-299 a month per supplier. $5-25k a year per buyer for dashboards and change alerts. Enterprise connectors later.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: Existing tools are sold to buyers and force suppliers into each buyer's portal. A supplier-owned credential flips the network effect, like a Plaid for origin. The USTR note on smaller suppliers signals regulators want a reusable format.
ideas.first_30_days: Target one cluster, such as 40 suppliers of one mid-size OEM in Monterrey/Laredo or Ohio. Get that OEM's buyer to say it will accept the passport. Build LLM extraction for mill certs. Onboard manually and aim for 10 paying suppliers.

ideas.title: Outside-Processing Milk Run for Job Shops
ideas.one_liner: Scheduled pickup routes and batching software for the heat-treat, plating and anodize bottleneck behind reshored machining.
ideas.customer: 10-100 person machine shops and fabricators, plus special-process houses (heat treat, anodize, plating, passivation, paint) that want fuller batches.
ideas.problem: As machining orders rise (machinery jobs +6.1k in August, record capital-goods orders), the constraint moves downstream to special processes. Shops ship parts by carrier ad hoc, parts sit in queues, and paperwork gets lost. ISM supplier deliveries have slowed for eight straight months. Environmental cost and owner retirements limit new special-process capacity (my inference).
ideas.solution: Vans on fixed weekly or daily routes between shops and vetted process vendors. Batching gives vendors full loads. Barcode chain of custody carries cert paperwork (heat-treat charts, NADCAP status). A promised turnaround (for example 5 days) is tracked by software.
ideas.why_now: Reshoring in existing walls raises job counts while outside-process capacity has not grown. Slowing deliveries make lead time visible.
ideas.revenue_model: Per-stop fee plus 8-12% margin on outside-processing volume. Vendor SaaS. Later, acquire a heat-treat or anodize house.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: Outside processing often accounts for most of a job's elapsed lead time but only a small share of touch time. That bottleneck yields to logistics and batching, not new furnaces, and adding a van is cheaper than adding an oven.
ideas.first_30_days: Pick one region such as Grand Rapids, Greenville or Wichita. Interview 20 shops. Sign two heat-treat or anodize houses. Run a one-van pilot two days a week and charge per stop.

ideas.title: Mobile Cobot Safety Validation Lab
ideas.one_liner: A van-based lab that measures collision forces and signs off robot and cobot cells against the 2025 ISO 10218 revisions.
ideas.customer: Cobot distributors, integrators and 10-200 person manufacturers deploying cells. EHS managers and insurers are the second buyers.
ideas.problem: North American robot orders are broadening into semiconductors, pharma and food, and cobots are 15.4% of units. The 2025 revisions of ISO 10218-1 and -2 (which absorbed the collaborative guidance of ISO/TS 15066) require documented risk assessment and validation. Few engineers can do it, and force-measurement gear costs tens of thousands of dollars. Distributors skip validation and the liability lands on the shop and its insurer.
ideas.solution: A van with a calibrated force and pressure measurement device, safety-scanner zone tester and stop-time tester. Technicians validate on site (contact-force mapping by body region, speed and separation checks) and deliver a signed report. Software stores and versions results for audits. Annual revalidation is a subscription.
ideas.why_now: Revised standards are in force, robot demand is broadening to small shops and new sectors, and mobile manipulators are coming into plants.
ideas.revenue_model: $2.5-6k per cell validation. White-label contracts with distributors. About $1.2k a year for revalidation. Referral fees from insurers.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: The limiting step for small-shop robots is fear of liability, not price. A third-party validation stamp is what insurers and owners want, and distributors have the incentive to sell but not the independence or equipment to certify.
ideas.first_30_days: Rent or buy a used force-measurement device. Sign three cobot distributors. Complete a machinery functional-safety credential. Validate the first five cells at a discount.

ideas.title: Book-Not-Shop Roll-Up of Retiring Machine Shops
ideas.one_liner: Buy retiring shops' customer books, programs and drawings on earn-outs, then migrate the work to a partner network.
ideas.customer: Owners of 5-40 person machine shops aged 60+ who want a clean exit. The buyer's customers keep their supply.
ideas.problem: About 60% of US manufacturing firms have owners aged 55+, about 150k small and mid-size firms are near retirement, and customers often leave when the owner retires (per American Machinist and MMS). MMS admits no dataset exists. Existing buyers such as Compass Precision buy whole shops with real estate, iron and payroll, which is capital-heavy and risky.
ideas.solution: Buy only the customer relationships, drawings, programs, fixtures and quality records for about 1-1.5x annual gross profit, paid mostly as an earn-out on retained revenue over 24-36 months. The owner runs a transition site for 6-12 months. Work then moves to 3-5 partner shops that have spare capacity. Equipment is auctioned or leased. AI digitizes quote history and setup sheets.
ideas.why_now: The retirement wave is under way and PMI at 55.6 (highest since May 2022) keeps demand steady. PE roll-ups have proven that a market exists, and a capital-light structure fits smaller teams.
ideas.revenue_model: 15-25% gross margin on migrated work. Slotting fees from partner shops. Deal capital is $250-750k per deal, mostly as earn-out.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: The asset is customer trust and tacit programs, not buildings or machines. An earn-out tied to retained revenue makes both sides fight the main failure mode of roll-ups, which is customer attrition.
ideas.first_30_days: Build a list of 300 target shops from state registries, LinkedIn and outreach. Sign three LOIs on owner-friendly terms. Line up three partner shops with capacity. Raise a $1M search-fund-style pool or use SBA financing.

ideas.title: Auto-to-Defense Conversion Accelerator for Tier-2 Suppliers
ideas.one_liner: A fixed-price certification package plus matched RFQs that turn idle auto-parts plants into qualified defense and aerospace suppliers.
ideas.customer: Tier-2 and tier-3 automotive stampers, machiners and casting shops with 25-250 employees in the Midwest and South. Defense primes co-fund supplier development.
ideas.problem: OEM robot orders are down 25% and autos lost 4.5k jobs in August, while defense money is flowing (Hadrian raised $1.37B; it holds an $80M Army deal). Auto suppliers have capacity and process discipline (IATF), but defense work needs AS9100, ITAR registration, DFARS specialty-metals tracking and NIST 800-171 and CMMC Level 2 (phase 2 is scheduled for November 2026). Consultants sell these piecemeal.
ideas.solution: A 90-day package: gap assessment, IATF-to-AS9100 crosswalk, ITAR registration, an NIST 800-171 plan on a managed enclave, DFARS specialty-metals tracking, and a mock audit, delivered mostly by templates and a small compliance team. It ends with RFQs matched from primes looking for capacity.
ideas.why_now: The auto retreat leaves capacity idle, defense capital is at record levels, and CMMC requirements are phasing in. Primes need more sub-tier suppliers.
ideas.revenue_model: $35-80k fixed fee per shop or $3-5k a month for the managed enclave. Success fee on first contract. RFQ-routing fees from primes.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: Auto suppliers already have the hard part (process discipline, volume) but are invisible to primes for lack of paperwork. Selling capacity conversion instead of compliance opens the prime's supplier-development budget. The CMMC consultant market is crowded, so the wedge is the RFQ match, not the audit.
ideas.first_30_days: Recruit five shops through chambers of commerce, auto-supplier associations and state MEP centers. Partner with a C3PAO and a GCC High MSP. Meet two primes' supplier-development teams about co-funding. Land two paid pilots at about $25k.

ideas.title: Made-in-USA Proof Files for Relabeling Brands
ideas.one_liner: Audit-ready substantiation files and monitoring for brands rushing to claim 'Made in USA' after tariffs.
ideas.customer: Consumer and industrial brands with $5M-$300M revenue and retailer private-label teams, buying through general counsel or the ecommerce head.
ideas.problem: Tariffs make US-made claims valuable, but an unqualified 'Made in USA' claim needs 'all or virtually all' US content and processing under FTC rules, with civil penalties per violation and state-law class actions on top. Brands switch suppliers on cost and forget the claim. Suppliers cannot document origin per component.
ideas.solution: Software plus service that maps each SKU's BOM to component and labor origin, gathers supplier attestations and mill certs, scores the claim, drafts compliant packaging and listing language ('Assembled in USA with global parts', or percent US), monitors marketplace listings and supplier changes, and builds a defense binder.
ideas.why_now: A reshoring marketing wave, supplier switching under tariffs, and active enforcement risk. The same BOM data that supports tariff compliance supports the claim.
ideas.revenue_model: $3-15k per product-line audit plus $500-2k a month for monitoring. Retailer programs that require proof.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: The first legal casualty of the reshoring wave is the label. Brands that reshore partially and market fully carry hidden liability, and a file built once serves both marketing and customs defense. The buyer is legal or marketing, not customs, so this avoids the crowded tariff-software budget.
ideas.first_30_days: Scan Amazon 'Made in USA' listings for weak claims using public data. Send a three-page claim risk scorecard to the brands. Sell the first 10 audits at $3k with a partner advertising lawyer signing off.

ideas.title: Resin Swap Bureau for Shortage-Hit Molders
ideas.one_liner: Fast material-equivalency testing and paperwork for injection molders who must switch resin grades when supply breaks.
ideas.customer: Small and mid-size injection molders and extruders with 10-200 employees, and their OEM quality engineers (appliance, auto, medical, electrical).
ideas.problem: Hormuz transits run about 10 a day against a baseline of 88-130, and the Gulf is a large polymer and petrochemical exporter (my inference on resin exposure). ISM comments cite long lead times and price volatility. Molders forced to change resin need to requalify with UL recognition, food-contact letters, PPAP and customer sign-off, and testing labs take weeks.
ideas.solution: An equivalency database (datasheet parsing plus coupon results) and a fast-turn lab partner. For each part spec it ranks substitutes, runs a five-day test protocol (tensile, impact, heat deflection, melt flow, shrinkage, UL 94 screen, color), and produces the change package: process change notice, PPAP delta and customer approval draft. It tracks UL, FDA and REACH status.
ideas.why_now: The war shock and volatility force substitutions now, and lead times are stretching. Molders have no in-house materials engineers.
ideas.revenue_model: $2.5-8k per part-family qualification. About $6k a year for database and alerts. Margin on lab work.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: In a shortage, finding a substitute resin is easy because a distributor can suggest one. The bottleneck is proving to a customer's QA that the substitute is allowed. The valuable product is the paperwork.
ideas.first_30_days: Partner with a certified test lab. Sign five molders. Build the first 50 equivalency sets in one resin family (PP, ABS or PC) from public datasheets. Publish a free shortage swap guide to gather leads.

ideas.title: IEEPA Refund Ledger for CPAs and Controllers
ideas.one_liner: An accounting workbench that turns IEEPA refund data into correct inventory, cost-of-goods, tax and audit entries.
ideas.customer: CPA and advisory firms serving importers, and controllers at $10M-$500M manufacturers and distributors.
ideas.problem: About 330,000 importers paid about $166B on 53M entries. CBP had repaid about $86.3B by 2026-07-10, and AD/CVD and liquidated-entry cases come later. Each refund must be split between duty still in inventory, duty already in cost of goods sold, and interest, each with different book and tax treatment (UNICAP, state conformity, LIFO layers). CFOs have no playbook and brokers do not touch accounting.
ideas.solution: Import ACE entry-summary exports and broker data. Match each entry line to inventory layers or sales. Compute period-by-period reversal entries. Produce journal entries, a tax memo, a state schedule and a reconciliation to CBP statements. Model cash-tax timing for Q4 estimates. Export to QuickBooks, NetSuite and Sage.
ideas.why_now: Refunds are flowing in phases now, with year-end close and Q4 estimated payments (due 2026-12-15 for calendar-year C corporations) approaching.
ideas.revenue_model: $750-3k per client engagement through CPA firms. $15-40k a year for white-label licenses. It grows into a standing duty sub-ledger for Section 232 changes.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: A refund is an accounting event, not a customs event. Every refund creates an inventory-basis and tax problem the broker will not touch, and the same ledger becomes the duty sub-ledger firms need as Section 232 rates keep changing.
ideas.first_30_days: Approach 10 CPA firms with importer clients. Build an Excel and Python prototype on three real entry datasets. Sell the first engagements at about $1.5k. Have a tax partner review the methodology.

ideas.title: Origin Assay: Forensic Testing of Metal Melt Origin
ideas.one_liner: A lab test that says where steel or aluminum was actually melted, so US-melt claims stop resting on paperwork alone.
ideas.customer: Importers and fabricators claiming the 10% US-melt rate, steel service centers selling premium 'US-melt' stock, customs counsel and insurers defending CBP audits, and buyers with domestic-metal requirements.
ideas.problem: Section 232 rates now depend on melt or smelt origin: 10% with US-melted metal against 25-50%. The certificate is worth thousands of dollars per ton, mill test reports can be relabeled or forged, and CBP is prioritizing origin verification and AD/CVD evasion. No independent test exists.
ideas.solution: Build a reference library by buying coupons from about 100 mills worldwide. Measure trace-element, inclusion and slag chemistry, and isotopic signatures (LIBS, ICP-MS, SEM-EDS). Train a classifier to give origin probability. First product is a mail-in Origin Assay with a confidence-scored report and sampling protocol built for audits. Handheld screening is a later roadmap. Classifier accuracy is the central risk, so start with one narrow discrimination, such as US EAF versus Chinese plate for one grade.
ideas.why_now: The 2026 tiers turn a chemistry fact into a financial asset. Cheaper mass spectrometry and machine learning make library-based classification plausible, and academic provenance work exists but no commercial library does (verify).
ideas.revenue_model: $300-900 per sample. $25-100k annual audit programs for service centers. Insurer verification programs. Later, handheld subscriptions.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: Duty policy turned melt origin into money, and paper certificates invite cheating, so the arbitrage is proof. Scrap-based EAF steel carries a fingerprint of tramp elements and alloy history that makes origin partly knowable.
ideas.first_30_days: Interview three service centers and three customs counsel. Buy or borrow about 40 heats of known origin (A36 and 304). Use a university ICP-MS lab to test discriminating power on two grades. Sell a $5k pilot verification of 10 suspicious heats.

ideas.title: Craft Data: Retiring Machinists Teach Robots
ideas.one_liner: Pay shops to let experienced craftspeople wear cameras and gloves, and sell the captured factory-floor skill data to robot-learning labs.
ideas.customer: Robot foundation-model and humanoid companies buying training data. Shops are the second customer, receiving cash and auto-generated standard work instructions.
ideas.problem: Physical AI funding hit $18.6B in Q2 2026, but labs lack high-quality real-world industrial manipulation data (setups, fixturing, deburring, measuring by feel). Meanwhile a retiring workforce takes unrecorded tacit skill, and no dataset of it exists.
ideas.solution: An egocentric capture kit (head and wrist cameras, instrumented glove, audio narration) worn during normal work. Add job context from CAM programs and travelers. Deliver curated, annotated datasets to labs. Shops receive setup videos, SOPs and a training library, and workers share in revenue, with consent, IP and safety protocols agreed up front.
ideas.why_now: Record physical-AI funding, cheap wearable capture hardware, imitation-learning advances, and a retirement wave. Labs need real industrial data, not lab data.
ideas.revenue_model: Target $150-400 per curated hour from labs (to validate with first buyers). Pay shops about $40 an hour. $500 a month per shop for the SOP and training library.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: The scarce input to robot learning is expertise, not compute. The same footage is a shop's best defense against retirement knowledge loss, so shops will host the capture and even pay for the by-product.
ideas.first_30_days: Recruit five shops with free SOP videos as the hook. Capture 100 hours. Pitch five labs with samples. Aim for one paid pilot of $20-50k. Hire an employment lawyer for consent and IP terms.

ideas.title: Tariff Forward Curve for Section 232 Lists
ideas.one_liner: A probability feed for which HTS codes join the next Section 232 lists, with parametric hedges to follow.
ideas.customer: CFOs and sourcing heads at importers with metal-heavy lines and $20M-$1B revenue, and trade counsel. Insurers and MGAs later.
ideas.problem: Firms treat tariffs as unpredictable, so they pre-buy a year of inventory or freeze decisions. But Section 232 additions run through a public administrative pipeline of industry petitions and comment periods (the latest request for comments on 2026-08-06). Other actions carry visible dates: polysilicon at 15% with minimum import prices from 2026-12-04, and a robotics and machinery investigation still pending. Nobody publishes odds.
ideas.solution: Model each HTS-10's probability and timing of inclusion or rate change using past inclusion rounds (petitioner identity, domestic producer concentration, import share, comment volume). Update as dockets move. Deliver a dashboard, API and Slack alerts. Phase 2 is a parametric cover with an MGA or event-contract venue that pays if a heading's rate rises by a set amount within 12 months, priced off the curve.
ideas.why_now: With IEEPA gone, Section 232 is the main channel. The inclusion process is open and docketed, LLMs can read comments at scale, and event-contract and parametric markets have grown.
ideas.revenue_model: $1.5-5k a month subscription. Later, commission or spread on hedges.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: Insiders call tariffs political noise, but 232 additions follow petitioners who show up months earlier. Even 65% accuracy is worth far more than the fee to a firm deciding whether to pre-buy. Tracking current rates is crowded, but forecasting future inclusion is not.
ideas.first_30_days: Scrape BIS inclusion dockets and Federal Register notices. Hand-label the last two rounds. Publish a free weekly 'next 232 list watch' newsletter. Sign five paid pilots from importers with more than $500k of metal-derivative exposure.

ideas.title: Pattern-Less Foundry Network via Printed Sand Molds
ideas.one_liner: Print sand molds centrally and pour them at idle small foundries to deliver castings in about two weeks with no patterns.
ideas.customer: Pump, valve, ag-equipment and machinery OEMs and repair shops needing 5-500 castings. Small foundries are the supply side.
ideas.problem: Small-lot castings from Asia now face tariffs and freight up to 50% higher. Domestic foundries quote long lead times, largely because of pattern-making and minimum runs, and aging owners are retiring or closing. Castings are an invisible bottleneck under reshoring and under Section 232 derivative rates.
ideas.solution: A hub with binder-jet sand printing (or rented capacity at existing bureaus) prints mold and core packages from customer CAD plus solidification simulation. Ship them to 10-30 small foundries that pour iron, steel or aluminum. The network handles NDT, dimensional checks and certs, including melt origin. Start with one or two alloys and repair and replacement parts.
ideas.why_now: Printed sand has improved in cost and speed, tariffs and freight punish imported castings, foundries are consolidating, and simulation and AI gating design are cheap.
ideas.revenue_model: Per-casting pricing with 25-35% gross margin. $500-3k engineering fee per part. Foundries pay for mold volume routed to them.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: The bottleneck is patterns and scheduling, not melting. Many small foundries have idle furnace hours but no digital front door, and a printed mold is a universal interface. US-melt certification is a sales kicker, not the core.
ideas.first_30_days: Sign three foundries with idle capacity. Buy printed molds from an existing bureau. Take 10 orders for obsolete pump or gearbox housings at $1-3k each, using 3D scans of broken parts.

ideas.title: Shopfloor Pulse: Voice-Agent Census of Job Shops
ideas.one_liner: Voice agents phone thousands of US machine shops monthly, publishing a real-time index of lead times, backlog and price pass-through.
ideas.customer: Macro and industrial hedge funds and alt-data desks, OEM sourcing chiefs and defense primes, PE and search funds hunting retiring owners, and regional economic developers.
ideas.problem: ISM surveys purchasing managers, not job shops, and MMS admits no dataset exists on shop ownership or retirement. Buyers cannot see real capacity or lead times, and funds rely on lagging government and PMI data despite July PMI at 55.6, prices at 71.1 and 12.64M jobs.
ideas.solution: Compliant, disclosed voice agents call about 3,000 shops a month with a four-minute script: quote lead time on a standard part, backlog weeks, materials surcharge, 5-axis or Swiss availability, and owner sale intentions. Combine with web and state-registry data. Publish a monthly index by region and process. Sell it as a subscription, and sell the resulting capacity directory to sourcing teams.
ideas.why_now: Voice models are cheap and natural in 2025-26, volatility makes non-consensus data valuable, and the retirement wave makes shop-level data valuable to buyers.
ideas.revenue_model: Alt-data subscriptions at $30-150k a year. Directory seats at $500-2k a month. Lead sales to search funds.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: The industrial base is tens of thousands of small firms nobody surveys, and the cost to survey them fell roughly 100x. A regional index that beats ISM by weeks is valuable because it is early, not because it is big. Telemarketing and TCPA rules need legal review, and calls should start human-assisted.
ideas.first_30_days: Build and legally review the script. Call 500 shops across three clusters. Publish a free preview index. Approach 10 alt-data desks. Aim for three paid pilots at $25-50k by month six.

ideas.title: Step-Down Club: Maintenance After the Max Dose
ideas.one_liner: A cheap maintenance membership that turns the majority of GLP-1 users who quit or plateau into a planned step-down and a monetizable restart.
ideas.customer: Adults 3-12 months into a cash-pay GLP-1 who have hit goal or are about to quit over cost (consumer pays); telehealths and pharmacies pay a bounty per verified restart.
ideas.problem: About one-third of non-diabetic obesity patients are still on therapy at 1 year. Stoppers regain roughly 4x faster than people who lost weight with behavior change, and ~60% of ex-users say they intend to restart. Every company optimizes for staying on the max dose, and nobody sells the middle path or owns the ex-user.
ideas.solution: At plateau, a physician-written protocol steps the user down to the lowest effective dose or a planned holiday. A connected scale plus waist and strength check-ins run on SMS. Pre-agreed regain triggers (e.g. +3% above nadir for 2 consecutive weeks) auto-route the user to the cheapest legitimate restart, such as a $149 pill program. Optional 'regain warranty' credit as an add-on.
ideas.why_now: SURMOUNT-MAINTAIN (Lancet, 2026) is the first RCT showing a reduced 5 mg tirzepatide dose kept about 70% of the weight loss (-16.6% vs -21.9% at max dose vs -9.9% on placebo). $149-$299 pills (Wegovy pill Jan 2026, Foundayo Apr 2026) make restart cheap. Telehealths are converging on the same price and now compete on acquisition cost.
ideas.revenue_model: $19-29/month membership, plus $75-150 partner bounty per verified restart or step-down conversion (a telehealth's first-fill CAC is est. $150-400), plus optional warranty add-on.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: Discontinuation is the modal outcome, not a failure mode. A restart is a lead worth more than the membership fee, so whoever owns the ex-user relationship owns the cheapest reacquisition channel in a market where every competitor sells the same drug at the same price.
ideas.first_30_days: Recruit 100 plateaued or ex-users from r/Zepbound, r/Semaglutide and Facebook groups. Have an obesity-medicine MD write the step-down and restart protocol. Run the check-ins on SMS with a BYO or $25 scale. Sign one telehealth or pharmacy partner for a per-restart bounty. Charge $19/month from day one.

ideas.title: Medicare-First Longevity Kit for Independent Practices
ideas.one_liner: Longevity medicine built on what Medicare already pays for, sold as a workflow kit to independent primary-care practices.
ideas.customer: Independent primary-care and DPC-adjacent practices (2-15 clinicians) with 500-2,000 Medicare patients each.
ideas.problem: The longevity boom (Function $2.5B, Neko ~$7B, Superpower up to $349/yr) targets cash-paying under-55s, while the highest-risk group, seniors, has a covered prevention stack that is badly under-used. Well under half of beneficiaries take the Annual Wellness Visit, and independents lack the workflow to turn covered services into a healthspan program.
ideas.solution: A configurable 'healthspan AWV' template with functional tests (chair-stand, grip, gait speed), cognitive and falls screens, covered lipid, diabetes and bone screening, and vaccine gap-closing. A monthly care-management billing layer (APCM codes introduced in 2025). Compliant ABN-based cash upsells for ApoB or Lp(a). Practices get scripts, patient handouts and a collections dashboard.
ideas.why_now: APCM monthly primary-care codes are new (2025). The Medicare GLP-1 Bridge began Jul 1, 2026, pulling seniors into metabolic care. Cash longevity prices keep rising, which cedes the 65+ segment. About 82% of doctors are employed, so the remaining independents are underserved by digital vendors.
ideas.revenue_model: $600-1,200/month SaaS per practice plus 15-20% of incremental collected revenue (est. $30-80k per clinician per year of newly captured billing).
ideas.non_obvious_insight: 'Longevity' for the 65+ is mostly a billing-and-workflow problem on already-covered benefits. Founders build for cash because that is where the venture buzz is, and they overlook the biggest and sickest demographic, whose payer is already at the table.
ideas.first_30_days: Recruit 5 independent practices via state IPAs and DPC-Medicare communities. Offer a free 30-day audit of their AWV and care-management capture, pulled from claims, showing dollars left on the table. Convert to a $499/month pilot with a success fee.

ideas.title: GLP-1 Palate Panel for Food R&D
ideas.one_liner: A managed panel of GLP-1 users and their households that food and restaurant companies rent to test products, portions and health claims.
ideas.customer: R&D and insights teams at mid-size CPG (protein, snacks, frozen), restaurant chain menu teams, foodservice for hospitals and senior living, and supplement brands that need claim substantiation ($25-150k per study).
ideas.problem: 73% of GLP-1 users report taste changes and 70% lose joy in eating, so 'just add protein' fails. About 70% change what the household eats, and non-users adopt 30-50% of the changes, so the affected base is ~50% larger than the user count. Food companies are reformulating and launching 'GLP-1 friendly' labels on general-population panels and conflicting forecasts.
ideas.solution: Recruit and maintain a segmented panel (drug, dose, weeks on therapy, aversion profile, household makeup). Run sensory, portion and format tests plus home-use tests and 8-12 week muscle and satiety claim studies. Deliver 'aversion maps' (which textures and smells trigger nausea at which dose) and household spillover models.
ideas.why_now: Households with a GLP-1 user doubled from ~11% to 22% in under 3 years. Pills launched in 2026 broaden the base. CPG is mid-reformulation, and FTC claim scrutiny makes 'evidence-backed' labels valuable. Purchase-panel incumbents see what is bought, not why.
ideas.revenue_model: $25-150k per study, plus $40-100k/year data subscription for 'aversion map' updates.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: The 'GLP-1 consumer' is 5-6 sensory segments that shift with dose and week on therapy, not one persona. Forecasting from sales data cannot separate them, but a panel can. The picks-and-shovels of a reformulation wave are the testers, not the brands.
ideas.first_30_days: Recruit 300 panelists from subreddits and Facebook groups with a $25 incentive, verified by photo of the pharmacy label. Publish a free 'taste change' survey report for press. Cold-email 30 CPG insights leads and land a first paid pilot of about $25k.

ideas.title: Independent Pharmacy GLP-1 Aftercare Studios
ideas.one_liner: A turnkey cash-pay aftercare membership that gives independent pharmacies their first PBM-free service line.
ideas.customer: Independent community pharmacies (~17k in the US). One report has ~41% not dispensing obesity GLP-1s in Q4 2025 over poor reimbursement.
ideas.problem: Insiders assume Walmart, CVS and Amazon win GLP-1 care because of scale. Independents get squeezed by PBM reimbursement below cost and skip the category, even though they see patients monthly and pharmacists can check dose, side effects and nutrition.
ideas.solution: A 'studio' kit: leased body-composition scale, a protocol (dose-step check, protein and strength plan, red-flag triage), scheduling and billing for a $39-59/month cash membership, and links to pill and vial cash-pay fulfillment. Includes collaborative-practice documents and, where state law allows pharmacist prescribing, protocols for it. Monthly outcomes report to the pharmacist and to referral partners.
ideas.why_now: $149-$299 cash pills remove the need for dispensing margin to justify the category. Lilly and Novo cash channels route through retail pharmacies. Big chains launched their own pharmacist support programs in 2026, so independents need a counter-offer.
ideas.revenue_model: $199-399/month SaaS per pharmacy plus 20% of membership revenue, plus device lease.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: GLP-1 is the first drug category where a pharmacy can earn from services with zero PBM exposure. Independent pharmacists are more trusted locally than a chain's app and have a natural monthly touchpoint.
ideas.first_30_days: Partner with one state pharmacy association or wholesaler buying group. Pilot in 5 pharmacies at $49/month. Track retention and a muscle proxy (grip and chair-stand) for the first cohort.

ideas.title: Turn Gray-Market Retatrutide Demand Into Trial Enrollment
ideas.one_liner: Intercept people searching to buy unapproved obesity drugs and route them, screened, to active trials that pay by the qualified referral.
ideas.customer: CROs, sponsors and trial sites running obesity and metabolic trials (paying per qualified lead or randomized patient), with the consumer as the traffic source.
ideas.problem: Sponsors struggle to recruit GLP-1-naive participants because prior GLP-1 use is an exclusion criterion and 22% of households already have a user. Meanwhile, non-trial retatrutide use grew ~1.8x per quarter, 71% of traced users bought outside trials, and Australia issued a liver and kidney injury alert in Jun 2026.
ideas.solution: A compliance-reviewed 'legitimate access' site and search and social funnel that meets intent ('retatrutide', 'triple agonist'), explains the risks, pre-screens (BMI, comorbidities, naive or washout status, geography) and refers to nearby enrolling Phase 2/3 sites. It screens out people who already took unapproved product where the protocol excludes them, and sponsors pay on qualified referral or randomization.
ideas.why_now: Retatrutide's Phase 3 program and Lilly's planned Q1 2027 filing are peak-hype. FDA and Lilly takedowns (>14,000 listings) push searchers toward risk. Pills at $149 are draining the classic trial pool, so recruitment cost per patient is rising.
ideas.revenue_model: Est. $150-500 per qualified referral and $2-6k per randomized patient, paid by CROs and sites, with performance tiers.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: Enforcement cannot remove demand. The highest-intent audience in obesity pharmacology is currently monetized by gray-market vendors, while trial sponsors pay per head for exactly the same people.
ideas.first_30_days: Build three landing pages and a screener reviewed by a regulatory consultant. Register with 3-5 enrolling sites and one CRO recruiter. Spend ~$3k on search and social ads for 'retatrutide clinical trial' style queries (check ad-policy limits) and deliver the first 50 pre-screened leads on a pay-per-qualified-referral contract.

ideas.title: Result-Loop Desk for Scan and Lab Startups
ideas.one_liner: An outsourced nurse-and-radiologist desk that closes the loop on abnormal results from full-body scans, MCED tests and mega-panels.
ideas.customer: Mid-tier consumer diagnostics operators without downstream care: full-body MRI resellers, regional imaging centers, longevity clinics, mega-panel labs and employer executive-health programs.
ideas.problem: A review of 12 studies found 95% of asymptomatic people had at least one abnormal whole-body MRI finding and 91% of those were not clinically relevant (15-30% false-positive rate). Primary-care waits average ~31 days, so patients arrive at their PCP with printouts. Adoption is accelerating (Neko $700M for a NYC launch, Function 1M+ members), and Lp(a) testing hit a wall when Lp(a)HORIZON failed on Sep 4, 2026, leaving many flagged people without a next step.
ideas.solution: Triage each flagged result (ignore, repeat in X months, refer), track follow-up imaging against nodule and lesion guidelines, produce a structured PCP handoff (FHIR), document loop closure and route to a price-transparent cash referral network. Sold as a risk-management service. Consumers can buy a $99 second-opinion review.
ideas.why_now: Elective screening boomed in 2025-26 (Function-Ezra, Neko US launch, MCED tests despite NHS-Galleri missing its primary endpoint in May 2026). Medscape and radiology press now describe a 'medical cascade', so reputation and liability risk are becoming visible to operators.
ideas.revenue_model: $40-150 per flagged member (B2B), plus annual tracking fee per incidental finding, plus consumer second-opinion upsell.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: Screening companies are paid at the scan, but the costs of false positives and lost follow-ups land months later on nobody. Because they are not care providers, they cannot build the follow-up function in-house, so it converts to a compliance product.
ideas.first_30_days: Sell a pilot to three regional imaging centers or longevity clinics that resell whole-body MRI. Staff one part-time radiologist and one RN navigator, run follow-up tracking with SMS and a spreadsheet, and charge $75 per flagged patient. Publish a 'follow-up leakage' audit as the sales asset.

ideas.title: Right-Size Rx: Deprescribing After GLP-1 Starts
ideas.one_liner: Pharmacist outreach that adjusts insulin, sulfonylureas and BP meds in the weeks after a GLP-1 start, sold to payers on avoided harm and drug spend.
ideas.customer: Medicare Advantage plans, Medicaid MCOs, ACOs and self-funded employers with large diabetic and hypertensive populations.
ideas.problem: Tirzepatide trial protocols recommend cutting sulfonylureas by at least 50% and basal insulin by at least 20% at start, because GLP-1 weight loss lowers glucose and blood pressure. In real practice nobody is triggered or paid to do this, so patients face hypoglycemia, hypotension and falls, while brand diabetes drugs (SGLT2s, DPP-4s) keep getting refilled.
ideas.solution: Claims-triggered (and pharmacy-partner-triggered for cash-pay fills) pharmacist outreach at days 7-28 after first fill among patients on insulin, SU or antihypertensives. Collaborative-practice protocols to adjust or recommend changes, home BP and CGM review, and a savings and safety ledger for the payer.
ideas.why_now: The Medicare GLP-1 Bridge started Jul 1, 2026 and cash pills at $149-$299 are pushing GLP-1s into older, more medicated patients. Payers are fixated on the GLP-1 price line and are missing the neighboring drug lines.
ideas.revenue_model: $2-4 per targeted member per month, or $250 per completed episode, plus a share of measurable avoided ED visits and drug savings.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: The near-term safety and cost of GLP-1s sits in the other drugs on the patient's list. Payers can offset part of the GLP-1 cost by trimming those, so it belongs on a CFO's line item, not just a quality dashboard.
ideas.first_30_days: Approach one regional MA plan or IPA and one pharmacist group. Run a 90-day pilot on 300 patients identified from Rx claims. Measure interventions made, hypoglycemia events and avoided fills, and hand back a savings ledger.

ideas.title: Pre-Procedure GLP-1 Readiness for Endoscopy and Ortho
ideas.one_liner: A 7-day workflow plus day-of gastric ultrasound that stops GLP-1 patients from being cancelled or aspirating at surgery centers.
ideas.customer: GI endoscopy centers, orthopedic groups, ASCs and their anesthesia groups.
ideas.problem: ASA reversed course in Oct 2024 and now advises most patients to continue GLP-1s, shifting the risk to residual gastric contents on the day. Centers cancel or abort cases, and 38% of GLP-1 users vs 8% of non-users were malnourished before joint surgery, which raises complication risk. There is no standard workflow, so every center improvises.
ideas.solution: Automated intake (drug, dose, indication, GI symptoms), tailored liquid-diet and hold instructions aligned to multi-society guidance, a malnutrition screen with a protein prehab plan, and nurse-performed gastric POCUS with AI-assisted antral grading and documentation on the day. Priced per case.
ideas.why_now: With ~22% of households containing a user, this is routine, not exceptional. Gastric POCUS studies are appearing (2025-26) and centers are looking for a defensible protocol after the 2024 guideline change.
ideas.revenue_model: $60-150 per GLP-1 patient case, plus anesthesia-group license and ultrasound rental.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: Centers will not stop scheduling GLP-1 patients, so the value is avoided same-day cancellations (thousands of dollars each) and defensible documentation. The buyer is the center's operations and anesthesia leadership, not the drug companies.
ideas.first_30_days: Sell to one endoscopy center and one anesthesia group. Supply paper-plus-SMS intake, protocols, a rented handheld ultrasound and training. Track cancellation rate before and after and price at $75 per case.

ideas.title: Disordered-Eating Tripwire for GLP-1 Prescribers
ideas.one_liner: A cheap, documented eating-disorder screen and escalation network embedded in GLP-1 telehealth intake.
ideas.customer: White-label medical groups that supply prescribers to many telehealth brands, GLP-1 telehealths, med spas and their malpractice carriers.
ideas.problem: GLP-1 use was ~50% among binge-eating-disorder patients and ~42% among atypical anorexia patients (JAMA Psychiatry 2026), and an NEJM 2026 perspective warned about masking and worsening disordered eating in telehealth. An investigation tied four white-label medical groups to ~30% of telehealth firms receiving FDA warning letters, and MDL 3094 has 4,700+ cases pending. Plaintiff lawyers and boards look for the next vector, and no screening or monitoring layer exists.
ideas.solution: A 3-minute validated screen (SCOFF or EDE-Q short form) inside intake, 2-question monthly check-ins, rules-based escalation to a network of ED-trained dietitians and therapists, and an exportable audit trail for boards and insurers.
ideas.why_now: FDA sent 30 letters in Mar 2026 and 25 in Jun 2026. Regulators, boards and carriers are moving to documented safeguards. The data showing high GLP-1 use in eating-disorder populations is new in 2026.
ideas.revenue_model: $3-6 per screened patient, $40-80 per escalation (paid by the prescriber or referral network), and a malpractice-carrier discount program.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: In white-label telehealth, liability concentrates in the medical group that sits behind dozens of brands, so a cheap, documented safeguard is standard-of-care insurance. ED providers also need referral flow, so escalation pays for itself.
ideas.first_30_days: Pitch two mid-size white-label groups or a 20k-patient telehealth. Deliver via an embeddable link, run 500 screens, and publish flag-rate benchmarks. Recruit 10 ED-trained clinicians for escalation.

ideas.title: GLP-1 Size-Curve Index for Apparel Planners
ideas.one_liner: A monthly 'size-shift index' that tells merchandise planners, airlines and furniture makers how GLP-1 adoption is moving their customers' bodies.
ideas.customer: Merchandise planners and size-curve analysts at apparel, footwear and outdoor brands and off-price retailers, plus airline, cruise, furniture and medical-equipment planners.
ideas.problem: Households with a GLP-1 user doubled to ~22%, and users lose double-digit percentages of body weight in a year. Retailers still plan size curves on last year's sell-through, which lags, causing markdowns on the wrong sizes. CFOs are already modeling downstream effects (Jefferies estimates ~$600M/yr airline fuel savings).
ideas.solution: Build an index by region, age and gender from licensed or partner data (pharmacy-fill proxies where affordable, retailer size and returns data, sizing surveys, public health data) and forecast size-curve migration by category. Deliver an API, a quarterly briefing, and a custom-model add-on.
ideas.why_now: Adoption accelerated after the 2026 pill launches. BCG and GoodRx data show measurable spend shifts (less pasta and bakery, more fragrance, skincare and supplements), so consumer-goods planners are hunting for leading indicators.
ideas.revenue_model: $40-120k/year per retailer or brand, plus $20-60k custom-modeling projects.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: Sell-through is a lagging indicator, and the drug adoption curve by ZIP is a leading one. It is a healthcare-adjacent data business with no clinical regulation if built on aggregated data, so a two-person team can sell it to non-healthcare budgets.
ideas.first_30_days: Build v0 from public data (NHANES, BRFSS, Google Trends) plus a 2,000-person sizing survey. Email 30 planners with a free size-shift report for one category and offer partner-data-in-exchange pricing. Sign one $15k pilot.

ideas.title: Medicaid Exemption Evidence Packs for FQHCs
ideas.one_liner: An EHR-connected engine that packages state-accepted exemption evidence (medically frail, SUD treatment, disability) so providers keep patients enrolled.
ideas.customer: FQHCs, safety-net hospitals and Medicaid MCOs in the 41 expansion states.
ideas.problem: Work requirements start Jan 1, 2027 (80 hours a month). Self-attestation is allowed only in 2027 and documentation tightens Jan 1, 2028, with 5.5-6.3M projected coverage losses and a 12.5-14.2% operating-margin hit for hospitals in expansion states. Clinical exemption evidence sits in provider EHRs but nobody packages it for state portals.
ideas.solution: Identify likely-exempt patients from problem lists and encounters, generate state-specific attestation and documentation packets, track renewal and verification dates, and give financial counselors a dashboard and patient outreach texts. Wedge is the clinical side, not the state's income-and-hours verification.
ideas.why_now: The CMS final rule and state notice deadlines (Aug 31, 2026) are done and system build is underway, so providers have about 3 months of runway. Patient-facing startups exist, but provider-side exemption evidence is mostly open.
ideas.revenue_model: $3-8 per covered high-risk member per month, or $75-150 success fee per retained member (an FQHC visit under PPS pays far more than a sliding-fee uninsured visit).
ideas.non_obvious_insight: States and their vendors handle income and hours data. The medically-frail and treatment-participation evidence lives with providers, and each retained Medicaid patient is worth many times the fee.
ideas.first_30_days: Sign 3 FQHCs in one state through the primary-care association. Manually pull 500 patients' problem lists and produce exemption packets. Measure approval rates, then automate state by state.

ideas.title: Peptide Assurance Mark for Clinics and Processors
ideas.one_liner: Independent lot testing and supplier audit with a QR-verifiable mark that lets peptide sellers pass payment-processor and insurer underwriting.
ideas.customer: 503A compounding pharmacies, peptide and longevity clinic chains, and the payment processors and insurers who need evidence to underwrite them.
ideas.problem: HHS moved ~14 of 19 Category 2 peptides (BPC-157, TB-500, GHK-Cu and others) back toward compoundable in Feb 2026, and an FDA panel backed BPC-157 and KPV on Jul 23. Clinics are multiplying, but Stripe and card networks exclude the category and Forbes (Jun 30, 2026) called it a '$1 billion industry banks won't touch'. Losing a merchant account kills sellers faster than FDA action.
ideas.solution: ISO 17025 lab partners test identity, purity, endotoxin, sterility and potency per lot. Supplier and chain-of-custody audits feed a public registry and QR verification that processors, insurers and state boards can accept, with annual certification and monitoring.
ideas.why_now: The legal window opened in 2026 with no infrastructure. Purity is uneven, and processors need third-party evidence to underwrite certified merchants.
ideas.revenue_model: $250-600 per lot test, $5-15k/year certification, and processor referral fees for certified merchants.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: The bottleneck is payments and insurance, not FDA. A credible independent mark is the key that unlocks mainstream merchant accounts, so processors are the hidden buyer.
ideas.first_30_days: Contract an accredited lab and run a blind-purchase audit of 30 popular BPC-157 and GHK-Cu products, published as a report. Sell $500 audits to 10 clinics and approach two high-risk processors about fast-tracking certified merchants.

ideas.title: Roll-Up of Compounding-Stranded Weight-Loss Clinics
ideas.one_liner: Buy distressed med spas and weight-loss clinics that lost their compounded GLP-1 margin, and convert them into aftercare-plus-aesthetics businesses.
ideas.customer: The clinics' patients, who pay memberships and procedures. Sellers are owners of weight-loss clinics, med spas and telehealth shells.
ideas.problem: FDA proposed excluding semaglutide, tirzepatide and liraglutide from the 503B bulks list on Apr 30, 2026 and sent ~55 warning letters to telehealth firms in Mar and Jun. Reportedly ~60% of med spas offered GLP-1 programs by 2025, many on compounded supply that peaked at ~30% of US volume. Owners want out, yet PE physician-practice deals are down ~50% in 2026, so buyers are scarce.
ideas.solution: Acquire 10-20 clinics at 0.3-0.8x revenue with seller notes and earn-outs. Convert to branded pill and vial cash programs, plus aftercare (muscle, nutrition, dose step-down), legal peptide offerings and aesthetics upsells. Centralize the medical director, billing and marketing.
ideas.why_now: The compounding cliff has stranded assets that are just patient relationships and licenses, while buyer capital retreated. 63% of 'Ozempic face' patients are cosmetic-clinic first-timers, so aesthetics cross-sell is real.
ideas.revenue_model: Clinic revenue of $199-399/month memberships plus procedures. Target ~25% EBITDA after integration, with a shared-services center.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: Distress plus absent buyers means near-free customer bases, and revenue per patient can rise after the switch to branded drugs plus aftercare. Earn-outs limit downside if patients churn.
ideas.first_30_days: Pull state med-spa and pharmacy lists and Instagram GLP-1 advertisers. Contact 100 owners, sign 2 LOIs with seller notes, and close the first acquisition of $150-300k with an integration playbook.

ideas.title: Sleep-Apnea-to-GLP-1 Pathway for DME Suppliers
ideas.one_liner: A co-management service that lets sleep labs and CPAP suppliers prescribe, retest and retain patients as they lose weight.
ideas.customer: Independent sleep centers, home-sleep-test companies and DME suppliers whose profit engine is CPAP resupply.
ideas.problem: Zepbound was approved for moderate-to-severe obstructive sleep apnea in adults with obesity on Dec 20, 2024, and Part D can cover it for OSA. As weight falls, patients drop CPAP without a retest or re-titration, and the DME loses resupply revenue and the patient. Sleep clinics have no pathway for prescribing or co-managing a drug.
ideas.solution: Baseline and 3/6/12-month home sleep tests, benefits verification and prior authorization for Zepbound-for-OSA, a nutrition and muscle plan, auto-CPAP pressure re-titration from device data, and a 'retest before you quit CPAP' protocol. DMEs keep the supply relationship where still needed.
ideas.why_now: The OSA indication now has Medicare and commercial coverage routes, and cash pricing is falling, so patient demand is arriving at sleep clinics without a pathway. DMEs see the threat and hold the patient data (CPAP usage) needed to co-manage.
ideas.revenue_model: $15-30 per patient per month to the DME or sleep center, or a share of retained resupply, plus per-test fees.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: The DME supplier looks like the loser but is the natural gatekeeper: it has adherence data, patient trust and a recurring billing relationship, and it will pay to convert lost resupply into a managed weight-and-airway program.
ideas.first_30_days: Approach 5 regional DMEs or sleep centers. Pilot on 100 CPAP patients with BMI of 30 or more and AHI of 15 or more. Measure PA success, retest rate and retained resupply.

ideas.title: GLP-1 Stipend-in-a-Box for Small Employers
ideas.one_liner: A counsel-reviewed HRA wrapper that lets small employers subsidize $149-$299 cash-pay GLP-1s with a capped monthly stipend.
ideas.customer: Employers with roughly 10-200 employees, sold through brokers, PEOs and HRA administrators.
ideas.problem: Large-employer coverage fell from 72% to 60% and more are dropping, while 27% of employers already point staff to LillyDirect or NovoCare. Direct-to-employer vendors like Waltz Health and 9amHealth target mid and large plans. Small employers can't carve out of a fully insured plan, and stipend plans raise ERISA, ACA and tax questions they can't answer.
ideas.solution: A packaged structure (QSEHRA, ICHRA or limited-purpose HRA, depending on group size) with plan documents, capped stipend rules, receipt-based reimbursement from DTC pharmacies, minimum-essential-coverage checks, and optional coaching. Brokers get a commission.
ideas.why_now: $149-$299 manufacturer cash prices make a capped stipend cheaper than open-ended coverage. Employers just dropped or plan to drop coverage before open enrollment, and TrumpRx and DTC channels launched in 2026.
ideas.revenue_model: $5-8 per employee per month plus ~5% of stipend flow, with broker commission share.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: The fight is over who administers the wrapper for the 90% of employers that PBM carve-out vendors don't serve. Compliance and broker distribution matter more than the coaching content.
ideas.first_30_days: Have an ERISA attorney draft the plan documents. Partner with an existing QSEHRA or HRA administrator. Pilot with 10 small employers (~300 lives) through two brokers and measure uptake and cost per participant.

ideas.title: N-of-1 Trial Network for the Peptide Boom
ideas.one_liner: IRB-supervised, blinded, randomized N-of-1 trials that let peptide users learn what works for them while building the missing evidence base.
ideas.customer: Consumers already using or considering BPC-157, TB-500, GHK-Cu or KPV (pay ~$249 per 12-week trial), plus clinics, 503A pharmacies, wearable and supplement brands that need substantiation.
ideas.problem: Peptides are legal-ish again (HHS Feb 2026; FDA panel Jul 23, 2026 backed BPC-157 and KPV despite agency concerns), yet there is no evidence base. Users self-experiment uncontrolled, clinics cannot substantiate claims, and the FDA panel itself flagged the gaps.
ideas.solution: A 503A pharmacy ships coded vials (active vs placebo, randomized crossover), an app collects pre-registered endpoints (pain scores, sleep, grip strength, wearable HRV) plus baseline and 8-week safety labs, and Bayesian analysis returns each person's answer and contributes to a public aggregated dataset. Start with BPC-157 for tendon and joint pain.
ideas.why_now: Peptide deregulation in 2026, cheap wearables and remote endpoints, AI-assisted protocol design and statistics, and a crowd of volunteers already injecting. N-of-1 designs need tens of people per question, not hundreds.
ideas.revenue_model: $249 per participant, $50-150k sponsor-funded studies from clinics and brands, and data licensing.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: When regulation retreats, credible evidence becomes the scarce good. The crowd already volunteers, and pre-registered N-of-1 series can outrun a traditional RCT for low-risk, subjective-endpoint questions.
ideas.first_30_days: Draft protocol and IRB submission with an FDA IND-exemption determination from counsel. Recruit ~60 people through biohacker communities and one partner clinic. Line up a 503A pharmacy for blinded placebo and open a $249 waitlist for the first cohort.

ideas.title: AI-Run Cardiometabolic Care at ACCESS Prices
ideas.one_liner: An AI-first, pharmacist-supervised chronic-care program engineered to profit at Medicare ACCESS payment rates that break human-coach models.
ideas.customer: CMS pays it as an ACCESS participant ($360 per beneficiary per year initially, $180 follow-on, with half withheld pending outcomes). Medicare beneficiaries enroll at no cost. Later Medicare Advantage and Medicaid plans pay.
ideas.problem: ACCESS launched Jul 5, 2026 with ~150 participants. Payment works out to ~$30/month and Omada and Hinge sat out, so incumbents' cost structures don't fit. Primary care cannot titrate hypertension, lipid and prediabetes meds for millions of patients at this price.
ideas.solution: A mailed validated BP cuff and scale, voice-AI check-ins, protocolized titration of low-cost generics (ARB or CCB, statin, ezetimibe, metformin) and low-dose oral GLP-1 maintenance. Pharmacist and NP co-sign changes, with autonomous renewals only where state sandboxes allow (Utah's Jan 2026 AI renewal pilot covers 190 meds but excludes injectables and controlled substances).
ideas.why_now: ACCESS is live with rolling cohorts and a Jan 1, 2027 start. Oral GLP-1s are now first-line accessible, real-time voice AI is deployable, and a state has legally let AI renew chronic prescriptions.
ideas.revenue_model: CMS outcome-aligned payments of $360/year initial and $180/year follow-on per beneficiary. Target unit cost under ~$150/year for 50%+ margin, plus outcome-linked upside.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: At $30 per member per month the winner is whoever gets cost per member under about $12/month, which is an AI-to-pharmacist ratio problem, not a product problem. Big digital-health brands are structurally excluded.
ideas.first_30_days: Confirm the current CMS application window for the Jan 1, 2027 cohort. Meanwhile pilot 200 cash or MA patients with cheap cuff kits through a partner pharmacy, measure BP control and unit cost, and recruit a pharmacist supervisor and medical director.

ideas.title: Voice-Agent Cash-Price Negotiator for Imaging
ideas.one_liner: AI voice agents that call 20-30 local facilities, negotiate a guaranteed cash bundle for an MRI, CT or scope, and book it for the newly uninsured.
ideas.customer: Uninsured and high-deductible patients (Urban estimates 4.8M newly uninsured after the ACA subsidy expiry; subsidy-cliff self-employed), small employers, and imaging centers, labs and ASCs with idle capacity.
ideas.problem: Posted prices are inconsistent and unusable, and cash prices for the same MRI can differ ~10x. Patients will not make 20 phone calls or negotiate, while facilities have idle slots.
ideas.solution: The patient submits an order. Agents call and email facilities for real quotes and slot availability, negotiate global-fee prepay bundles, filter for accreditation and quality, return one guaranteed price and book, with escrowed payment.
ideas.why_now: Real-time voice agents became reliable in 2025-26, and coverage loss is growing (ACA subsidies expired; Medicaid work requirements from Jan 2027). Posted-price marketplaces exist but they don't negotiate dynamically.
ideas.revenue_model: $19-39 per booked procedure plus a 5-10% fee from facilities filling otherwise idle slots (cash-pay only, structured to avoid federal-program referral issues).
ideas.non_obvious_insight: Cash price is a negotiated market for empty slots. Discovery cost used to be too high per patient, and voice agents make it nearly free.
ideas.first_30_days: Concierge 50 MRI, CT and colonoscopy quotes in one metro with call scripts and an LLM voice agent on top. Publish the price spread, sign 5 imaging centers, and charge $29 per booking.

ideas.title: Incretin-in-a-Drop Assay for Life Underwriting
ideas.one_liner: A dried-blood-spot or oral-fluid lab test that tells insurers whether an applicant is actually on semaglutide, tirzepatide, orforglipron or retatrutide.
ideas.customer: Life and disability insurers, reinsurers, MGAs and paramedical exam vendors, with bariatric programs, trial sponsors and outcome-based employer programs as follow-on buyers.
ideas.problem: Cash-pay and direct-ship fills (LillyDirect, NovoCare, telehealth-partner pharmacies, compounders, gray market) are only partly visible in claims-based Rx histories, so BMI looks 'preferred' while drug-supported. Stopping the drug means rebound and adverse selection. Gray-market retatrutide is invisible by design.
ideas.solution: A validated LC-MS/MS panel (semaglutide, tirzepatide, orforglipron, cagrilintide, retatrutide) run by a partner CLIA lab as an add-on to the paramedical exam, returning 'on-board, recent use or none'. Later expansions to pre-op verification, adherence-verified outcome contracts and a consumer 'proof of adherence' report.
ideas.why_now: Published LC-MS/MS methods for semaglutide and tirzepatide matured in 2026, the FDA's LDT rule was vacated in 2025, and cash-pay pill volume exploded in 2026 (Wegovy pill >2M scripts).
ideas.revenue_model: $25-45 per test as an underwriting add-on, volume tiers for carriers, and later $79 consumer or clinician tests.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: This is the first mass-market chronic drug that bypasses the industry's data plumbing. Underwriters will pay for direct measurement over questionnaires because the cost of a wrong mortality class is far above $35.
ideas.first_30_days: Ask two Rx-history vendors what share of DTC fills they see. Contract a CLIA tox lab to validate an assay from published methods. Pitch 10 MGAs and reinsurer innovation teams, and run a paid 200-sample blinded pilot with one friendly insurer, with consent and state unfair-discrimination rules reviewed by counsel.

ideas.title: Alcohol Bridge: GLP-1 Addiction Care for Hospitals
ideas.one_liner: A hospital-embedded service that starts naltrexone plus semaglutide at discharge for alcohol use disorder with PEth monitoring.
ideas.customer: Hospital addiction-consult teams and liver clinics, plus health plans and employers paying for alcohol-related admissions.
ideas.problem: Only ~2% of people with alcohol use disorder get medication. A Lancet RCT (May 2026, n=108) showed semaglutide cut heavy drinking days in AUD with obesity, with NNT ~4.3 vs 7+ for approved drugs, and NIH-reported work shows added benefit on top of CBT. Phase 3 trials and the VA's CRAVE trial are running, but clinicians have no protocol, and opioid bridge clinics got settlement money while alcohol, the bigger killer, got none.
ideas.solution: A bridge service at discharge: naltrexone alone or with semaglutide (per trial eligibility, BMI 30 or more), PEth blood monitoring every 4 weeks, telehealth follow-ups and a cash-pay pill pathway, with outcome reporting on readmissions and PEth negatives.
ideas.why_now: The first RCT and NIH coverage landed in 2026, GLP-1s are now cheap and familiar, and hospitals are under margin pressure from readmissions. Off-label use requires careful protocols, so first movers will set the standard.
ideas.revenue_model: $250-400 per patient per month billed to hospitals, payers or employers, plus grant and state SUD funds where eligible.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: Alcohol-related admissions repeat and cost the hospital, but no service line owns the medication step. The wedge is a discharge protocol, not a new clinic.
ideas.first_30_days: Approach 3 hospital addiction-consult teams and hepatology clinics. Recruit an addiction-boarded medical director and run a 30-patient quality-improvement pilot under the hospital's existing governance, charging a ~$20k pilot fee.

ideas.title: Fake-Citation Triage for Defendants Facing Pro Se Filings
ideas.one_liner: A same-day report showing which citations in an opposing pro se filing are fake, misquoted or overruled, formatted as a court-ready exhibit for a motion to strike or for sanctions.
ideas.customer: Repeat defendants that get flooded with self-represented suits: landlord and property-management litigation groups, employment-defense boutiques, university and hospital counsel, insurer claims-litigation units, debt servicers, city attorney offices and municipal risk pools. Paid by the litigation budget owner.
ideas.problem: Charlotin's database holds about 2,095 AI-hallucination cases as of 28 Sep 2026, and 1,208 (58%) involve pro se litigants versus 829 involving lawyers. Pro se filers are immune to bar discipline, sanctions ($1,750 to $23,222) are slow and rare, and the defendant pays $300-600/hour of associate time to hand-check dozens of cites. Every hallucination-checker on the market is pitched to the lawyer who erred.
ideas.solution: Drag-and-drop a PDF. The tool extracts citations (open-source eyecite plus CourtListener), resolves each one, and flags nonexistent cases, quotes that do not appear in the opinion, wrong court or year, and negative treatment. Output is a two-page 'Citation Defect Declaration' plus a draft paragraph for a motion to strike or a Rule 11-type motion.
